title: Alvin E. Lirio, MD, PhD
text:
I’m a physician-scientist with a PhD in genetic epidemiology. I use large-scale human genomics and statistical genetics to understand how genes, environment and lifestyle shape complex disease.

My work centres on genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and downstream analyses in large biobanks and population cohorts, bringing together genomic, clinical and lifestyle data to find disease mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets.
I trained as a doctor in the Philippines and practised as a general physician before moving into research. That clinical grounding, and my work with Filipino cohorts, drives a long-standing commitment to improving genomic representation of underrepresented populations.
I’m currently a Postdoctoral Research Associate at the Ulverscroft Eye Unit, University of Leicester, UK.

Interests

Respiratory and cardiometabolic population genetics
Longitudinal disease trajectories and gene-by-environment interactions (smoking, diet, lifestyle, medications)
Rare variant and non-coding variant analyses
Multi-ancestry genomics and underrepresented populations

title: Research
text: Using UK Biobank linked electronic health records, I ran a genome-wide association study of longitudinal FEV1 decline in people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, modelling lung function trajectories with conditional linear mixed models. (Manuscript under review.)

title: Research
text:
Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm)
As part of my PhD, I contributed to a GWAS of PRISm, drawing on the EXCEED cohort, published in the European Respiratory Journal (2023).

title: Research
section: Asthma genetics in a Filipino cohort
text:
Asthma genetics in a Filipino cohort
I led a candidate-variant association study of self-reported asthma in mothers of the Cebu Longitudinal Health and Nutrition Survey (CLHNS), one of the few long-running population cohorts in Southeast Asia (BMC Genomic Data, 2026).

title: Research
text:
Ocular genetics
At the Ulverscroft Eye Unit I run genome-scale analyses (GWAS, fine-mapping) in UK Biobank to identify genes and pathways behind ocular traits, working with ophthalmologists, statisticians and bioinformaticians. This includes work on the genetics of human foveal development (IOVS, 2025).

title: Research
text:
Type 2 diabetes in Filipinos
At the Institute of Human Genetics, National Institutes of Health Philippines, I worked on a UCSF collaboration on the metagenomic and genetic determinants of type 2 diabetes in Filipino populations, coordinating participant recruitment and phenotype collection.
